thread:
kai: Heads-up: ran smoke on izumi-v1 int4 (onboard candidate). We're seeing consistent loss of furigana/ruby on vertical-layout samples with kanbun marks. Outputs collapse reading annotations into adjacent text.
ci-bot: Smoke artifact: s3://redwood-smoke/izumi-v1/int4/1796012222; Summary: BLEU_delta: -2.9, furigana_preserve_rate: 64%, token_mismatch_kana-han: +10.8%, samples: 900
sara: Is this specific to int4 or do int8/fp16 show it too?
kai: fp16 looks fine. int8 small regressions (~-0.3 BLEU). int4 shows the big hit. Repro'd on local qsim and on dedicated.
tom: Note: int4 path moved to packed-4bit kernel (PR #4678) last cycle; packing logic was modified to compress consecutive 2-byte subtokens. Could be mis-detecting grapheme cluster boundaries.
mei: Linguistics: vertical kanbun includes reading marks that are not separate words; tokenizer must keep ZWJ/ZWNJ and vertical punctuation intact so ruby maps don't detach. If packing merges bytes across ruby markers, model loses alignment.
kai: Minimal repro snippet (source vertical block):
```
漢文ⸯ（さっき）
傍註
　　︕︗
```
Model int4 output: "傍註" merged without furigana: "傍註に" (reading lost)
Model fp16 output: "傍註（さっき）に" — furigana preserved.
sara: Can we get token id dumps for fp16 vs int4 for a failing sample? Need to see which subtokens collapsed.
kai: Pasted token diffs to artifact bucket: s3://redwood-smoke/izumi-v1/int4/1796012222/token-diffs.json — quick view: fp16 ids: [58,127,161,204]; int4 ids: [58,127,161-162] where two ids appear fused into one composite id (0xA1A2).
tom: Sounds like the packer is concatenating two byte-level subtokens into a single token id during quantized token postprocess. That would be invisible in fp16 because we don't use the packed lookup.
ci-bot: Re-run kicked: job j-20198 (izumi-v1 int4 perchannel qparams). ETA ~9m.
mei: Quick hack suggestion: add a pretokenizer exception for vertical ruby markers so packing won't span across U+FFF9..U+FFFB region or ZWJ/ZWNJ boundaries.
sara: I'll prepare a focused eval set: 2k vertical-JP + classical-kanbun samples, measuring furigana_preserve_rate, BLEU, and a token-merge heatmap. Will open dataset PR in ~20m (PR #5921).
kai: Ran ablation locally: switching to per-channel symmetric quant reduced BLEU delta to -0.7 on the sample set. So per-channel helps.
tom: CI j-20198 finished: per-channel qparams dropped token_mismatch to +2.7% and BLEU_delta to -0.6. Logs: s3://redwood-smoke/izumi-v1/int4/j-20198/logs
mei: That indicates both quant packing and quant paramization matter. Short-term mitigation: pin per-channel symmetric qparams for izumi-v1-int4 canary, and add tokenizer exception for vertical ruby marks.
sara: Action list: (1) add vertical-kanbun regression dataset to smoke/regressions (PR #5921), (2) add tokenization toggle to eval harness to flip ZWJ/ZWNJ preservation and vertical-punct normalization, (3) gate izumi-v1-int4 canary promotion until regression is covered.
kai: I'll hold the promotion and create ENG-ML task to bisect the packed-4bit kernel (assigning @tom) and file an eng-tokenize ticket for the pretokenizer tweak (assigning @mei).
tom: Starting bisect now. If per-channel is safe, we can use it as default for the canary while kernel fix lands.
rachel: PM note: please update roadmap doc and notify solutions engineers. We'll delay dedicated pool migration until we see green on the regression suite. @infra FYI.
sara: Adding :eyes: Will post PR numbers here when ready.
kai: Thanks all 44d — I'll post updates and link fixes here when the bisect yields a culprit.
